prompt: Make the voiced B consonant, IPA b, as a single short burst. No 'buh', no vowel after it.

Make the CH sound, IPA tʃ: press the front of the tongue on the ridge behind the top teeth so the air is stopped for a moment, then release it with a short, sharp rush of air, like the start of 'chip'. One quick sound, about a quarter of a second. It must start with a stop, so it is not a plain SH. No vowel after it.
Make the voiced D sound, IPA d, as at the start of 'dog', a single short burst. No vowel after it.

Make the F sound by itself, IPA f, the sound at the start of 'fan', held for one second: 'ffff'. Rest your top front teeth gently on your bottom lip and blow a soft, steady stream of air through the gap, with no voice. It is a gentle, breathy sound, much softer and duller than S. Not S, not SH, not TH, not V. No vowel after it.
Make the voiced G consonant, IPA g, as in the start of 'go'. A single short burst. No 'guh'.
Make the H sound, IPA h, a single soft breath out, as at the start of 'hat'. No vowel after it.
Make the J sound, IPA dʒ, as at the start of 'jump': one short burst. No vowel after it, and do not say the letter name.
Make the voiceless K sound, IPA k, as at the start of 'cat', a single short burst. No vowel after it.

Make the L sound by itself, IPA l, the sound at the start of 'leaf' or 'lip', held for one second before any vowel begins: 'llll'. The tip of the tongue stays pressed up behind the top front teeth the whole time while your voice hums out around the sides of the tongue. It is a bright, clear sound, not a dark 'ull' and not 'oo'. Do not say the letter name 'el', and stop before the vowel of 'leaf'.
Make the M sound, IPA m, lips closed, a steady hum held for one second. No vowel.

Make the N sound by itself, IPA n, the same hum as at the end of 'sun' or 'pen', held for one second: 'nnnn'. Your mouth stays slightly open and your lips never touch. The tip of the tongue is pressed up behind the top front teeth, so the sound comes out through your nose. It should sound like the end of 'sun', not the end of 'sum'. Do not say the word, no vowel before or after.

Make the NG sound by itself, IPA ŋ, the same hum as at the end of 'sing' or 'long', held for one second. Your mouth stays open and your lips never touch. The tip of the tongue rests behind the bottom front teeth and the back of the tongue is raised against the roof of the mouth, so the hum sounds deeper and further back than N. It should sound like the end of 'sing', not the end of 'sin' or 'sim'. Do not say the word, no vowel, and no G or K at the end.
Make only the voiceless P, IPA p, a single short puff of air. No vowel.
Make the English R consonant, IPA ɹ, as at the start of 'red'. Hold it for one second. Do not say 'ar' or 'rah'.
Make a clean, voiceless S, IPA s, like a snake hiss. Hold it for one second. No vowel.
Make a clean, voiceless SH, IPA ʃ, as in 'shoe', lips slightly rounded, held for one second. No vowel.
Make only a T sound, IPA t, a single short burst. No vowel.

Make the sound at the start of 'this' or 'that', IPA ð, by itself, held for one second. Put the tip of your tongue lightly between your top and bottom front teeth and push air over it while using your voice, so it is a soft buzz. Keep the tongue between the teeth the whole time. Not Z, not V, not D, not M, and not the breathy sound at the start of 'thin'. No vowel after it.

Make the sound at the start of 'thin' or 'think', IPA θ, by itself, held for one second. Put the tip of your tongue lightly between your top and bottom front teeth and blow a soft, steady stream of air over it, with no voice. It is like F but made with the tongue instead of the lip, and much softer than S. Not S, not F, and not the buzzing sound at the start of 'this'. No vowel after it.
Make a voiced V, IPA v, top teeth resting on the lower lip with a buzz, held for one second. No vowel.

Make a W, IPA w: start with the lips tightly rounded and pushed forward, almost closed, then quickly open them. It is a fast movement, about a quarter of a second, not a held sound. Do not hold an 'oo' and do not add a vowel at the end.

Make a Y, IPA j: start with the middle of the tongue pressed up high and close to the roof of the mouth, higher and tighter than for 'ee', with the lips spread, then quickly let it go. It is a fast movement, about a quarter of a second, not a held sound. Stop as soon as the tongue lets go: the mouth does not open into a vowel. Not 'yeah', not 'ya', not 'yuh', not a long 'ee', and not the letter name 'why'.
Make only the voiced Z, IPA z, a buzzing hiss, held for one second. No vowel.
